=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:380-394, 448-459 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A bare `git push origin HEAD` is checked against the literal branch name `HEAD` instead of the checked-out branch, so a push from a branch whose PR has merged can bypass the guard.
  WHY: The GitHub PR lookup for `HEAD` returns no match, allowing the push; all reviewers rated this BLOCKER.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:337-340, 348 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The assignment-prefix matcher does not recognize Bash `NAME+=value` assignments, so a guarded Git command following one can be silently skipped.
  WHY: The push or commit then runs without branch-status or ancestry checks; severity disagreement: deepseek and google rated this MAJOR, while openai, qwen, and z-ai rated it BLOCKER.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:405-410, 436 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: When `--repo` supplies the remote, `_push_targets` still discards the first positional argument as though it were the remote, dropping the first refspec from guard evaluation.
  WHY: A push can fall back to checking the current branch or skip checking a destination, especially in a detached worktree; severity disagreement: deepseek, google, and openai rated this MAJOR, while qwen rated it BLOCKER.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:249-270, 390-435 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: File-descriptor redirections such as `2>&1` leave the descriptor digit `2` in parsed push arguments, where it can be treated as a refspec.
  WHY: Resolving that invalid refspec can fall back to checking the session checkout instead of the worktree and falsely block a valid push; severity disagreement: deepseek and google rated this BLOCKER, while openai, qwen, and z-ai rated it MAJOR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:321-322 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The shell walker clears the resolved working directory after `||`, even when a successful `cd` means the later Git command runs in the worktree.
  WHY: The push is checked against the session checkout instead, which can falsely block a valid worktree push.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:255-263, 321-322 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Output redirection on a `cd` command is tokenized as a separate segment that clears the resolved working-directory context.
  WHY: A subsequent push is checked against the session checkout instead of the worktree and can be falsely blocked.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1313-1322 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The per-target loop can emit multiple permission-request JSON objects for one hook invocation when multiple target lookups fail.
  WHY: The hook harness expects a single JSON response object; severity disagreement: deepseek, google, and openai rated this NIT, while z-ai rated it MAJOR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS / _guarded_git_invocations | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: A subshell command such as `(cd /worktree && git push ...)` is not recognized as a subshell, so the Git command can be evaluated against the session checkout.
  WHY: The guard does not detect the unresolved subshell directory, which can leave a push unguarded or evaluate the wrong checkout.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_targets truncated long-option handling | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The accepted `--e` abbreviation is overly broad and may consume a refspec as an option value.
  WHY: A future Git push option beginning with `--e` could be misparsed, silently dropping a refspec from guard evaluation.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "If the directory cannot be resolved (a variable, a subshell), keep today's behaviour for that command and log a warning."
  expected_change_site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py, `_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS` and `_guarded_git_invocations`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS` does not include parentheses, so `(cd /worktree && git push ...)` does not produce a standalone `(` token; `_guarded_git_invocations()` therefore does not mark the subshell directory as unresolved or emit the required warning before checking the Git command from the session checkout.
- requirement: Tests in `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` cover acceptance cases and parser paths including bare `HEAD`, append assignments, `--repo`, subshells, and redirections.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The added tests cover worktree resolution, `cd`, `git -C`, and other listed cases, but do not cover append-assignment recognition; bare `git push origin HEAD`; `--repo` with refspecs; subshell commands; or file-descriptor redirections and affected shell operators.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_shell_segments_with_operators and _guarded_git_invocations, lines ~255-263 and ~321-322 (inserted code) | severity=high | confidence=[5]

  WHY: A later worktree push falls back to the session checkout and can be falsely blocked.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_evaluate_bash, ~lines 1290-1320 (inserted code) | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Multiple unreachable push targets can each print a permission-request JSON object.
  WHY: The hook harness expects a single valid JSON response object.

  Evidence of absence: `_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS = ";&|\n<>"` does not include parentheses, so `(cd /worktree && git push ...)` tokenizes `(cd` as one word; the subshell directory is not recognized and the required unresolved-directory warning is missing.
  severity=low | confidence=[5]
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Cover these cases in guard tests." The issue lists specific acceptance criteria: cd-based worktree, git -C, unresolvable directory fallback, explicit source tips, multiple destinations.
  Expected change site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff adds tests for worktree resolution, cd, git -C, GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, unresolvable fallback, and explicit tips, but no test covers append-assignment recognition.
  severity=low | confidence=[5]
